title: Zeroth Fitting ideal of a direct sum
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $M,N$ be finitely generated $R$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Write $I_0(P)$ for the zeroth kernel-minor ideal of a finite free surjection onto any finitely generated $R$-module $P$, independent of that surjection by [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change]. Then
$$I_0(M\oplus N)=I_0(M)I_0(N).$$

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07ZA (lemma-fitting-ideal-basics), part (2), the equality Fit_0(M direct sum N) = Fit_0(M) Fit_0(N).

proof.text: Choose finite free surjections π : R^n → M and ρ : R^m → N using Module.Finite.exists_fin'. Form q : R^(n+m) → M × N using finSumFinEquiv. Choose preimages separately to prove q surjective. Presentation independence identifies the three zeroth Fitting ideals with the ideals of these presentations. At k = 0, each column embedding is a permutation, so presentationFittingIdeal_zero_eq identifies the ideal with the span of determinants of square matrices whose rows lie in the kernel, including n = 0 via the empty determinant 1.

source.place: Tags 07Z8 (lemma-fitting-ideal), kernel-row description, and 07ZA (lemma-fitting-ideal-basics), proof of (2): the direct-sum presentation.

proof.text: For a kernel-row matrix B of q, write B = X + Y, where X has zero right block and Y has zero left block. Expand det B using Matrix.detRowAlternating.map_add_univ. A summand C has each row chosen from X or Y. If det C = 0 its membership is immediate. Otherwise the Leibniz formula has a nonzero term indexed by a permutation σ. Every entry C(σ j,j) is nonzero, hence σ sends the left column indices to rows chosen from X and the right column indices to rows chosen from Y. Thus C.submatrix σ id is block diagonal, with diagonal rows in ker π and ker ρ. Matrix.det_fromBlocks_zero₂₁ gives the product of two determinant generators. Matrix.det_permute changes det C by the unit sign σ; removing this unit proves that each summand lies in the product ideal. Summing proves the forward inclusion. This argument uses no domain hypothesis: it only uses that a product containing a zero factor is zero.

source.place: Tag 07ZA (lemma-fitting-ideal-basics), proof of (2), expanding the determinant calculation behind Tag 07Z7 (lemma-ideals-generated-by-minors), part (4).

proof.text: For determinant generators det A of the π-ideal and det D of the ρ-ideal, form Matrix.fromBlocks A 0 0 D. Reindex both rows and columns by finSumFinEquiv.symm. Each row lies in ker q, by the corresponding kernel condition and preservation of zero by the other map. Matrix.det_submatrix_equiv_self and Matrix.det_fromBlocks_zero₂₁ give determinant det A * det D. Ideal.span_mul_span and Ideal.span_le extend this to the reverse ideal inclusion. All constructions allow empty blocks and use the empty determinant convention, without finite generation of either kernel.

source.place: Tag 07ZA (lemma-fitting-ideal-basics), proof of (2), reverse inclusion in the block-diagonal maximal-minor calculation of Tag 07Z7(4), with empty blocks included.

proof_origin.place: Tags 07ZA(2), 07Z7(4), and 07Z8. The block determinant calculation is implemented by row multilinearity, a nonzero Leibniz term to arrange the blocks, and Mathlib block diagonal determinant and permutation formulas.
